name: Delaware
agency: Delaware Division of Motor Vehicles (DMV), Department of Transportation
permitAge: 16 (Level 1 learner's permit, ages 16 to 17; to 21 with an active IEP), after an approved driver education course (21 Del. C. 2710)

teen.supervisedHours: 50 hours, including 10 at night, certified by a parent or guardian before unsupervised driving
teen.holdPermit: Level 1 permit valid 12 months; first 6 months supervised only
teen.nightLimit: After the first 6 months: may drive alone 6 a.m. to 10 p.m.; 10 p.m. to 6 a.m. only supervised, except to and from work, church or school activities
teen.passengerLimit: During the permit year: no more than one passenger besides the adult supervisor (more allowed if immediate family, per DMV summary in secondary source)
teen.phone: All drivers: no hand-held electronic communication device while driving since 2011; hands-free calls allowed for adults. Under-18 rule not confirmed by a found source.

notes: Supervisor: licensed parent or guardian, or licensed driver at least 25 who has held a Class D license at least 5 years, in the front seat (session law, legis.delaware.gov Chapter 16448).
Knowledge test: commercial sites say 30 questions, 80 percent to pass; another says 20 questions, 75 percent. Not confirmed from DMV, so left null.
Official driver manual URL not found in search (state DMV domain not reachable from here). Spanish manual: unknown.
Move over (21 Del. C. 4134): change lanes away or slow down; a secondary summary says at least 20 mph below the limit where the limit is 50 mph or more. Not used in questions until checked.
Hand-held phone fine: $100 first offense per Office of Highway Safety (not used in questions).
